title: The Lantern Station Handbook

files.name: first-adventure.txt
files.title: The Lantern Station Handbook
files.description: A short dispatch handbook with three boats, explicit selection rules, and worked examples.

teachingGoal: Learn to apply several constraints to a choice, use a tie-break rule, and pause when required information is missing.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Which boat should carry a 1-kilogram parcel for Reed Island if it must stay dry?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Shelter. It visits Reed Island, supports up to 5 kilograms, and has a waterproof cover. Swift lacks the required cover.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Which boat should carry an ordinary 2-kilogram parcel to Reed Island?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Swift. Both Swift and Shelter qualify, but Swift has the smallest sufficient weight limit. Exactly 2 kilograms is within Swift's limit.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: What should happen to a parcel addressed to Mist Island?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Hold it for a supervisor. No listed boat visits Mist Island, so the source does not support assigning a route.

notes: Original fictional training material; not shipping advice.
The intended demonstration is a first source-to-game creation flow. The generated scaffold, story, and interface can vary.
A correct lesson should explain destination, weight, and dry requirements before asking learners to dispatch parcels.

title: The Cedar Workshop Access Desk

files.name: access-desk.txt
files.title: The Cedar Workshop Access Desk
files.description: A fictional role-and-approval policy with least-permission decisions and incomplete-request cases.

teachingGoal: Match a stated task to the smallest sufficient permission set and check the corresponding authorization independently.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: What role and approval does Maya need to edit a draft card?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Maker is the smallest sufficient role. Her complete request needs the project owner's approval.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Can Maya use her draft-editing approval to publish the corrected card?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: No. Publishing requires Steward and a new approval from the archive owner for that task.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: What three details must a request contain before the desk can grant access?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: The person's name, a concrete description of the task, and an end date. The applicable owner's approval is also required.

notes: Original fictional policy; not a real organization's security procedure.
The distinction between role suitability and approval is essential; neither check replaces the other.
A generated activity may classify requests or present decisions, but exact UI or template selection is not guaranteed.

title: The Riverglass Message Relay

files.name: systems-relay.txt
files.title: The Riverglass Message Relay
files.description: A simplified system model with four component responsibilities and a timestamped stale-cache investigation.

teachingGoal: Connect a symptom to the responsible component and verify a repair against the original observation.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Which component converts Bird Gallery into room code B7?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: The resolver. The router sends coded requests, the archive stores current official messages, and the cache stores temporary copies.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Why does the visitor at 10:05 still see 'closes at 4' after the archive changed at 10:03?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: The B7 cache copy created at 10:00 has a 10-minute lifetime and has not expired. An archive update does not immediately update an existing cache copy.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: What does clearing B7's cache entry change, and what stays intact?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: It removes the temporary B7 copy so the next successful request reads the current archive message. It does not delete B7 from the archive.

notes: Original simplified model; component rules apply to the fictional relay, not every real network.
A useful explanation should connect the timestamps to cache expiry instead of merely naming the cache.
The expected lesson is diagnosis and cause-and-effect reasoning; a specific systems game scaffold is not guaranteed.

title: The North Window Exhibit Record

files.name: evidence-desk.txt
files.title: The North Window Exhibit Record
files.description: Three fictional observations for comparing counts, percentages, unsupported causes, and missing evidence.

teachingGoal: Choose the right measure, explain the scope of evidence, and distinguish a supported answer from an unknown.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Which sign had the highest proportion of stopped visitors who followed the arrow?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Green: 8 of 10 stopped visitors, or 80 percent. Blue had 75 percent and Amber had 60 percent.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Which sign had the largest number of followers, and does that establish that its color caused more learning?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Blue and Amber tied at 9 followers. This does not establish a learning effect: learning was not measured, the signs appeared at different times, and comparable conditions were not established.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: How much did the Green sign cost to print?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: The source does not say. Printing costs are explicitly listed as missing information, so no amount can be supported from this record.

notes: Original fictional observations; not a real study or a general claim about behavior.
This kit is suitable for comparing Aster's local source lookup with optional AI explanations. Local lookup may return relevant passages rather than calculate a conversational answer.
An honest unknown on the printing-cost question is a successful evidence boundary, not a requirement to invent an answer.

title: The Pine Trail Supply Challenge

files.name: supply-run.txt
files.title: The Pine Trail Supply Challenge
files.description: An exact-number planning puzzle with essential kits, optional bonuses, a coin budget, and a time budget.

teachingGoal: Satisfy mandatory requirements first, add independent resource totals, and compare feasible optional choices.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: What does one water kit, one food kit, and one blanket kit cost in total?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: 9 coins and 5 turns. Those three kits completely supply both explorers, leaving 3 coins and 3 turns.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Which feasible bonus earns the most points after buying the essentials?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: The signal earns 5 points. Including essentials, it costs 12 coins and 7 turns, staying within the limits of 12 coins and 8 turns.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Why can the team not add both field notes and marker repair after the essentials?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Those two bonuses together cost 4 coins, but only 3 coins remain. Their combined time fits the remaining 3 turns, but the coin limit still rules the pair out.

notes: Original tabletop rules, not outdoor safety or provisioning advice.
Kits cannot be split and each purchase is allowed at most once; those constraints must survive generation.
The highest-scoring result is fully determined by the source, while its visual or gameplay presentation can vary.

title: The Pocket Garden Explorers

files.name: young-explorers.txt
files.title: The Pocket Garden Explorers
files.description: A clear, concrete two-property sorting exercise for readers around ages 8–10 using invented seeds and beds.

teachingGoal: Match two properties, notice how one changed property affects a decision, and recognize when no option fits.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Where does Glowbud belong before any screen is added, and why?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Sunny Bed, because Glowbud needs bright light and dry soil, and Sunny Bed has both.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Where should Duskdot go before the screen changes Sunny Bed?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: The waiting shelf. Duskdot needs low light and dry soil, and none of the three original beds has that combination.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Which seed fits Sunny Bed while its screen is in place?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Duskdot. The screen changes Sunny Bed to low light while the soil stays dry. Glowbud no longer fits because it needs bright light.

notes: Original invented plants and needs; not gardening advice.
An adult can choose the child's age group in Asterloom and review generated reading level and instructions before play.
Age selection should not be presented as a guarantee that an AI-generated game is suitable without review.

title: The Maple Library Rule Update

files.name: two-sources-handbook.txt
files.title: The Maple Library Lending Handbook · Version 1
files.description: The original fictional lending policy, effective 1 September. Add this source first.

files.name: two-sources-update.txt
files.title: The Maple Library Lending Update · Version 2
files.description: An explicit 1 October update changing exactly two rules and preserving the others. Add this source when rebuilding.

teachingGoal: Reconcile a scoped update with an earlier source, preserve unchanged facts, and apply the correct rule for an effective date.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: On 5 October, may a standard member who already has 3 books borrow one more?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Yes. Version 2 replaces the former 3-book limit with a 4-book limit on and after 1 October.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Does Version 2 change the youth member's book limit or allow youth map-set loans?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: No. Youth members may still hold at most 2 books, and they still may not borrow map sets. Those Version 1 rules were not replaced.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: What loan periods apply to map sets checked out on 28 September and 5 October?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: The 28 September loan keeps its original 7-day period. The 5 October loan uses the new 10-day period. The update does not retroactively extend existing loans.

notes: Original fictional library rules; not a real library policy.
Begin with Version 1 alone if demonstrating an existing game; add Version 2 before starting an AI rebuild.
Both sources should remain available after the update so learners can trace which facts changed and which stayed the same.
Do not claim that an existing game's lessons update automatically when a source is added; recreate or rebuild the lessons with AI.

title: The Small Exhibit Handoff

files.name: transcript-trail.txt
files.title: The Small Exhibit Handoff · Written Transcript
files.description: An original timestamped meeting transcript containing roles, dependencies, checks, an example, and an unaccepted suggestion.

teachingGoal: Extract the agreed process from conversation, distinguish suggestions from decisions, and send a failed check back to its responsible stage.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: What is the agreed stage order and who owns each stage?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Draft: Claire. Review: Evan. Print: Theo. Install: Evan. Each next stage waits for the preceding stage's completion checks to pass.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Is blue paper a requirement?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: No. Claire suggests blue paper at 02:19, but Rowan explicitly says at 02:27 that paper color has not been chosen.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: What should happen if a printed card has a clipped word?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Return to printing: Theo reprints the card and repeats the print check. The transcript says not to change the approved wording to fix this print failure.

notes: This downloadable file is an original written TXT transcript. It does not include an audio or video recording.
Timestamps support locating evidence but do not imply a playable media attachment.
Users can apply the same learning-source approach to their own authorized transcript; transcription of an uploaded recording may involve additional dependencies.

title: The Three-Stop Coastal Survey

files.name: offline-expedition.txt
files.title: The Three-Stop Coastal Survey
files.description: Three connected investigations that can support a multi-part game and a clear save-and-resume check.

teachingGoal: Apply a tie-break, resolve uncertainty with a bounded second reading, and leave an evidence-backed record for continuation.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Which original channel should the cart use at Pebble Gate?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Channel 1. Channels 1 and 3 are open, and the rule chooses the lowest-numbered open channel.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: What should happen if Mirror Pool shows amber and then amber again?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Report that the result remains uncertain. Do not continue or keep taking readings until a favorable one appears.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Which flag wins at Wind Post and why?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: East. East and West tie for the greatest count at 7, and East comes first alphabetically among the tied flags.

notes: Original fictional survey rules; not a coastal or outdoor safety guide.
Creation requires an AI connection; the completed game can be used to check local play after disconnecting AI or going offline.
The source provides three distinct learning segments, but the number and names of generated missions can vary.
Use the main desktop player's saved progress for the continuity check; do not imply progress sync between different player implementations.

title: The Paper Bridge Design Lab

files.name: pass-it-on.txt
files.title: The Paper Bridge Design Lab
files.description: A design catalog and two briefs that make a source-grounded game understandable, shareable, and easy to adapt.

teachingGoal: Compare alternatives against multiple constraints and preserve assumptions so another learner can understand or revise a decision.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: Which design fits the original 12-centimeter gap, 3-counter load, and 5-credit budget?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Folded Deck. Its 15-centimeter span and 4-counter capacity meet the requirements, and its cost of 4 credits is within budget.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: What changes if the gap becomes 18 centimeters and the budget becomes 6 credits?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: Arch Deck becomes the valid choice. Folded Deck is too short, while Arch Deck spans 20 centimeters, supports 5 counters, and costs 6 credits.

expectedEvidenceChecks.question: What if the gap is 18 centimeters but the budget stays at 5 credits?
expectedEvidenceChecks.answer: No listed design fits. Flat Deck and Folded Deck are too short, and Arch Deck costs more than the budget.

notes: Original fictional model properties; not engineering advice for a real bridge.
The intended demonstration is exporting one completed notebook, opening it as a recipient, and optionally adapting its sources in the full app with AI.
Keep the catalog unchanged when trying the alternate brief so the effect of changed requirements remains visible.
Share only material you have rights to distribute and retain the Asterloom license in the exported package.
